Short-interval repeats rarely resolve p-tau217 gray zones

In 92 paired samples, Lumipulse p-tau217 had ICC 0.94 and within-person CV 11.2%; 8% crossed one probability boundary, and averaging duplicate samples did not reduce the indeterminate group.

Key quantitative results: Core biomarkers showed Spearman ρ at least 0.80 and ICC at least 0.92. Lumipulse p-tau217 had Spearman ρ 0.95 (95% CI 0.92–0.97), ICC 0.94 (95% CI 0.90–0.96), and within-subject CV 11.2% (95% CI 9.2–13.2%).

BiomarkersBloodp-tau217Brain-derived p-tau217Repeat testing

Added October 28, 2026 · DOI:10.1186/s13195-026-02180-8

Evidence summaryDesign, results, and what changed

Thirty-second field brief

The study supplies practical repeatability estimates for three plasma platforms. Lumipulse p-tau217 was highly reliable, yet 8% of participants crossed one low/indeterminate/high boundary. Repeating and averaging the sample did not shrink the gray zone, arguing against routine short-interval duplicate testing as a fix for borderline results. Ratios also did not uniformly improve reliability.

Study design

Paired plasma samples from 92 participants were collected a median 85 minutes apart, with a range of 30 minutes to 92 days. The cohort included 22 patients with AD, 8 with other neurodegenerative disease, 27 asymptomatic autosomal-dominant AD mutation carriers, and 35 controls. Lumipulse p-tau217 was available in 92; NULISAqpcr core biomarkers in 80; and 132 NULISAseq measures were assessed.

Key quantitative results

  • Core biomarkers showed Spearman ρ at least 0.80 and ICC at least 0.92. Lumipulse p-tau217 had Spearman ρ 0.95 (95% CI 0.92–0.97), ICC 0.94 (95% CI 0.90–0.96), and within-subject CV 11.2% (95% CI 9.2–13.2%).
  • NULISAqpcr brain-derived p-tau217 had ICC 0.95 but higher within-subject CV of 22.0% (95% CI 17.6–26.5%); its Aβ42 ratio reduced CV only modestly to 21.1% and did not improve reliability.
  • Across NULISAseq, 101 of 132 analytes had within-subject CV below 20%; Aβ42/40 improved reliability over Aβ42 alone, although their CVs were similar at 12.5% and 13.0%.
  • Using Lumipulse thresholds below 0.153, 0.153–0.422, and above 0.422 pg/mL, 7 of 92 participants (8%) crossed one category boundary between samples.
  • Averaging the paired p-tau217 results did not reduce the indeterminate category; the mean absolute difference was 15.8%, supporting limited value for routine short-interval repeat sampling.

What changed

The paper quantifies short-interval variation for current Lumipulse and NULISA platforms and directly tests whether duplicate p-tau217 sampling resolves classification uncertainty. It generally does not.

Strength of evidence

Moderate analytical and biological-variability evidence with paired within-person measurements and platform-specific estimates. Precision is limited by the 92-person mixed cohort, small diagnostic subgroups, heterogeneous sampling intervals, and lack of clinical-outcome validation.

Clinical and field impactInterpretation, implementation, and access

Clinical significance

A result close to a cutoff can cross categories because of ordinary short-interval variation. Routine immediate retesting or averaging should not be assumed to resolve the gray zone; discordant and borderline cases still need clinical review and an assay-appropriate confirmatory strategy.

Field medical relevance

Directly informs repeat-testing policy, cutoff uncertainty, gray-zone workflows, ratio interpretation, biological variation, and cross-platform implementation of blood biomarkers.

Quanterix or platform relevance

Reliability was platform- and analyte-specific. Lumipulse p-tau217 showed lower within-person variability than NULISAqpcr brain-derived p-tau217, while the NULISAseq panel reports relative NPQ units that limit direct numerical comparison with absolute-concentration assays.

Access or reimbursement relevance

Avoiding low-yield duplicate sampling could reduce cost and delay, but the study creates no coverage, reimbursement, authorization, or availability change.

Likely questionsWhat you may hear and what the evidence supports
Should every indeterminate p-tau217 result be repeated immediately?
The study does not support that as a routine solution: averaging two short-interval measurements did not reduce the indeterminate group.
How stable was Lumipulse p-tau217?
Reliability was high, but within-person CV was 11.2% and 8% crossed one category boundary.
Do ratios always improve repeatability?
No. Aβ42/40 improved reliability versus Aβ42 on NULISAseq, but brain-derived p-tau217/Aβ42 did not materially improve reliability on NULISAqpcr.
Critique and limitationsBias, uncertainty, and missing evidence
  • Only 92 paired participants and 80 on the low-plex panel
  • Small and clinically heterogeneous diagnostic groups
  • Sampling intervals ranged from 30 minutes to 92 days
  • No amyloid-PET or CSF reference standard for category changes
  • Relative NULISAseq units limit direct cross-platform comparison
  • No patient-outcome or prospective repeat-testing utility trial
